proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
S=\{v\in V:|\operatorname{pa}_D(v)|=2\},
\qquad h=|S|,
\]
and introduce pairwise distinct vertices \(R=\{r_v:v\in S\}\) disjoint from \(V\). Define
\[
\widetilde V=V\mathbin{\dot\cup}R,
\qquad
\widetilde D=D\cup\{(r_v,v):v\in S\},
\qquad
\widetilde B=B.
\]
In the last equality, \(B\) is viewed as a set of pairs contained in \(V\), so every pair containing a new vertex is absent from \(\widetilde B\). In the vertex order \(V,R\), define
\[
\widetilde\Sigma=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&0\\
0&I_h
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Because the input lies in the promise domain of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\), \(\Sigma\) is rational, \(\Sigma\succ0\), and \(\mathcal F_G(\Sigma)\ne\varnothing\), by \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\). The construction appends at most \(n\) vertices and uses only entries from \(\{0,1\}\) outside the supplied matrix, so its output size and running time are polynomial in the binary input length. Rationality of \(\widetilde\Sigma\) follows immediately.

For any nonzero \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^h\), positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\) gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}
\widetilde\Sigma
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}
=a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a+b^{\mathsf T}b>0.
\]
Thus \(\widetilde\Sigma\succ0\). If \(\Sigma\) is strictly diagonally dominant, each old row of \(\widetilde\Sigma\) has the same diagonal entry and the same sum of absolute off-diagonal entries as before, while each new row has diagonal entry one and off-diagonal absolute row sum zero. Hence strict diagonal dominance is preserved.

Every matrix supported on \(\widetilde D\) has a unique block representation
\[
\widetilde L=
\begin{pmatrix}
L&0\\
U&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
U_{r_v,j}=
\begin{cases}
u_v,&j=v,\\
0,&j\ne v,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(L\) is supported on \(D\). Direct block multiplication using \(\mathrm{def:fiber}\) yields
\[
I_{n+h}-\widetilde L=
\begin{pmatrix}
I_n-L&0\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
(I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)^{\mathsf T}
\widetilde\Sigma
(I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)
&=
\begin{pmatrix}
(I_n-L)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-L)+U^{\mathsf T}U&-U^{\mathsf T}\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}\\
&=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Omega(L)+U^{\mathsf T}U&-U^{\mathsf T}\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For each \(v\in S\), the pair \(\{r_v,v\}\) is absent from \(\widetilde B\). The corresponding missing-bidirected-edge equation is therefore
\[
0=\bigl[(I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)^{\mathsf T}
\widetilde\Sigma(I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)\bigr]_{r_v,v}
=-U_{r_v,v}=-u_v.
\]
Hence every \(\widetilde L\in\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)\) has \(U=0\). Conversely, if \(U=0\), the old--old block in the displayed product is \(\Omega(L)\), every new--old off-diagonal entry is zero, and the new--new block is \(I_h\), whose off-diagonal entries are zero. The fiber definition consequently gives the exact equivalence
\[
\widetilde L\in\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
U=0\ \text{ and }\ L\in\mathcal F_G(\Sigma).
\]
Thus restriction \(\widetilde L\mapsto L\) is a bijection with inverse
\[
L\longmapsto
\begin{pmatrix}
L&0\\
0&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In particular, the enlarged fiber is nonempty. Since the queried edge \(e\) is an old edge and its coefficient is unchanged under the two inverse maps, \(\mathrm{def:attainable\mbox{-}set}\) implies
\[
\mathcal A_e(\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma)
=\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma).
\]

It remains to check the graph restrictions. The component hypothesis implies that \(G\) is acyclic of depth one and has maximum directed outdegree one. Each new vertex is a root having exactly one outgoing edge, so the construction preserves all three properties. Every old vertex of indegree two receives exactly one new parent and therefore has indegree three; vertices of indegree zero or one are unchanged; and new vertices have indegree zero. Consequently
\[
\max_{v\in\widetilde V}|\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde D}(v)|\le3,
\qquad
K_{\widetilde G}
=|\{v\in\widetilde V:|\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde D}(v)|=2\}|=0.
\]
The inequality, rather than equality, is necessary when \(S=\varnothing\). Each two-parent in-star becomes a three-parent in-star on four vertices, while isolated vertices and single directed edges are unchanged. Hence every directed weak component has at most four vertices. All asserted properties follow, and the exact equivalence of fibers shows that no singular or exceptional branch has been discarded.

By \(\mathrm{thm:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}completeness}\), there is a promise-preserving polynomial-time many-one reduction from the \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete complemented planted-selector language to \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\). For every promised source instance \(Q\), its output \((G_Q,\Sigma_Q,e_Q)\) has rational strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite covariance, a nonempty fiber containing the supplied rational witness, directed depth one, maximum directed outdegree one, and directed weak components that are isolated vertices, single directed edges, or two-parent in-stars.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}to\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}zero\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}padding}\) to this output. It produces \((\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q,e_Q)\) in deterministic polynomial bit complexity. The corrected conclusion of that lemma gives
\[
\max_{v\in V(\widetilde G_Q)}
|\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde D_Q}(v)|\le3,
\qquad K_{\widetilde G_Q}=0,
\]
and preserves acyclicity, directed depth one, maximum directed outdegree one, rationality, positive definiteness, strict diagonal dominance, and feasibility; in particular, the rational feasible witness supplied by the compiler extends by setting every new coefficient to zero. Its component analysis shows that every directed weak component of \(\widetilde G_Q\) is an isolated vertex, a single directed edge, or a three-parent in-star. The exact restriction bijection preserves the queried coefficient and therefore gives
\[
\mathcal A_{e_Q}(\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q)
=\mathcal A_{e_Q}(G_Q,\Sigma_Q).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\), the padded triple lies in the promise domain of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\), and either triple is a YES instance precisely when its displayed attainable set is a singleton. Thus the composition of the compiler with the padding map is a promise-preserving many-one reduction to the stated \(K_G=0\) subclass of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\). The source equivalences in \(\mathrm{thm:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}completeness}\) and the equality of attainable sets show explicitly that
\[
Q\in\mathsf{coSEL\mbox{-}PNQF}
\Longleftrightarrow
\mathcal A_{e_Q}(\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q)=\{0\},
\]
whereas
\[
Q\in\mathsf{SEL\mbox{-}PNQF}
\Longleftrightarrow
\mathcal A_{e_Q}(\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q)=\{0,1\}.
\]
This proves \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness on the stated subclass. Because the padding establishes equality of complete fibers before taking the queried projection, the reduction preserves singular fibers and uses no genericity, rank, division, or limiting condition.

For membership, \(\mathrm{lem:published\mbox{-}numedge\mbox{-}bounds}\) places unrestricted promised numerical edge identification in \(\forall\mathbb R\). For a fixed \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), the additional condition \(K_G\le k\) is decidable from the directed adjacency matrix in polynomial time: compute every directed indegree and count those equal to two. Restricting a promise problem in \(\forall\mathbb R\) by such a polynomial-time decidable promise condition leaves it in \(\forall\mathbb R\). Hence numerical edge identification on the literal class \(K_G\le k\) belongs to promise \(\forall\mathbb R\). Since the hard family just constructed has \(K_G=0\), it belongs to \(K_G\le k\) for every \(k\in\mathbb N_0\). Therefore the restriction is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete for every fixed \(k\).

Finally, suppose there were an exact algorithm on the literal parameterized class with bit complexity \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(N)\), where \(N\) is the total binary input length. On the hard family, \(k=0\), so the running time would be \(f(0)\operatorname{poly}(N)\), a polynomial because \(f(0)\) is constant. Promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness would then give \(\forall\mathbb R\subseteq\mathsf P\). The reverse inclusion follows directly from the universal-real decision model, since a polynomial-time decision may be performed before outputting a fixed true or fixed false quantifier-free sentence. Thus \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).

The obstruction in \(\mathrm{def:parameterized\mbox{-}handle}\) is exact: when \(K_G=0\), the handle exposes no coefficient entering a two-parent vertex, but the padded instance can still contain three-parent vertices and retains a fiber bijective to the hard source fiber. The separately displayed zero-two-parent hardness statement is precisely the \(k=0\) special case of the present all-fixed-\(k\) result, rather than an independent hardness phenomenon.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \((G,\Sigma,e)\) be a triple in the promise domain underlying \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\), and suppose that every directed weak component of \(G\) is an isolated vertex, a single directed edge, or a two-parent in-star. There is a deterministic polynomial-bit transformation producing \((\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma,e)\) such that \(\widetilde G\) is acyclic of depth one, has maximum directed indegree at most three, maximum directed outdegree one, directed component size at most four, and \(K_{\widetilde G}=0\); moreover, \(\widetilde\Sigma\) is rational and positive definite, and it is strictly diagonally dominant whenever \(\Sigma\) is. Restriction to the original vertices is a bijection \(\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)\to\mathcal F_G(\Sigma)\), and hence
\[
\mathcal A_e(\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma)=\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma).
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The premise allows an instance with no two-parent vertex. Then the padding set is empty and the output maximum directed indegree can be zero or one, so equality to three is false; the construction always proves the required upper bound of at most three while preserving every other conclusion.

prose_updates.tldr: A covariance-specific coefficient can be generically recoverable yet ambiguous or singular at the supplied covariance. Maximum directed indegree one is the exact tractable side: a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm normalizes every bi-affine fiber into pole-aware Möbius components and a singular-relation \(2\)-CNF, returning a unique rational coefficient, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. At indegree two, promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness already holds for depth-one directed graphs whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single edges, or two-parent in-stars. A separate exact-fiber padding converts that hard family to graphs of maximum directed indegree at most three with \(K_G=0\), so the literal class \(K_G\le k\) remains promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete for every fixed \(k\); the displayed \(k=0\) theorem is its special case. The private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler is exactly fiber-bijective and has rational strictly diagonally dominant covariance. Dörfler et al. already provide fiber bijectivity; the strict hard-side delta is replacing their shared unbounded-fan-in storage star by components of size at most three.

project_justification.gap: Complete low-fan-in algorithms are generic and may divide by expressions that vanish at the observed covariance. Dörfler et al.'s numerical-hardness construction already gives an exact fiber isomorphism in the rational feasible acyclic mixed-graph class, but its single storage sink has directed fan-in growing with the source dimension; it does not establish hardness on bounded-size directed components. The proposed residual parameter \(K_G\) also counts only vertices of indegree exactly two and therefore does not control higher fan-in.
project_justification.niche: The missing case is an all-covariance, polynomial-bit classification at fan-in one paired with a fiber-faithful lower bound at the next integer fan-in, already on depth-one private-parent components of size at most three, together with an exact audit of whether counting only two-parent vertices yields a useful residual parameter.
project_justification.fill: The Möbius-component and singular-clause normal form proves exact tractability with checkable componentwise-quadratic certificates. The private-slot compiler replaces the published unbounded storage star by singleton and two-parent sinks, preserves the complete source fiber through forced occurrence hubs, and yields promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness with rational strict diagonal dominance and a planted rational feasible matrix. A polynomial-bit padding preserves the entire fiber while replacing every two-parent sink by a three-parent sink; hence \(K_G=0\) on the padded hard family and the literal class \(K_G\le k\) is complete for every fixed \(k\).

prose_updates.related_work: Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz define numerical edge identification at a feasible covariance, prove unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness, and already construct an isomorphism from their source solution set onto the complete real SEM fiber. Their Section 4 uses a shared storage sink with one incoming coefficient per source coordinate. The hard-side strict delta here is only the replacement of that unbounded-fan-in star by depth-one private-parent directed components of size at most three while retaining exact fiber bijectivity; rational strict diagonal dominance and a supplied planted witness are normalization properties. The fan-in-one theorem separately tightens their polynomial-space upper bound on that restricted class. The exact padding result further shows that the literal parameter counting vertices of indegree exactly two is already zero on an at-most-three-parent hard family; the zero-parameter statement is the \(k=0\) special case of the theorem for all fixed \(k\), not a separate discovery. Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz derive missing-cycle quadratic equations and document spurious-root behavior. Gupta and Bläser, followed by Briefs and Bläser, give complete generic algorithms for tree-shaped models; their Möbius and rank analysis informs the pointwise normalization but does not cover exceptional supplied covariances. Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant study graph-wide global identifiability, and Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the half-trek sufficient criterion for generic rational identification. Ankan, Wortel, Bollen, and Textor connect graphical identification to the MIIVsem workflow, which remains the primary numerical-identification consumer here. Robust recovery, regular half-trek inference, and covariance-confidence-set inversion remain secondary and are not consequences of the exact fiber theorems.
prose_updates.interpretation: The result is a pointwise statement about the structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\), not a claim that a generic formula is numerically safe at every covariance. The observed-law functional is the attainable set \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\); the fiber-reduction lemma proves that it equals the set of queried coefficients across all compatible SEM parameterizations, so identification means that this set is a singleton. Fan-in one permits a complete exact audit with constructive low-degree certificates. At fan-in two, hardness persists even though every directed component contains at most one sink and two private roots, so neither long directed paths nor large directed components causes the obstruction. Moreover, padding each two-parent sink with one forced-zero private parent preserves the exact fiber and produces an at-most-three-parent hard family with \(K_G=0\). Thus \(K_G\) is not a distance-to-fan-in-one parameter on the literal class: its all-fixed-\(k\) completeness theorem is the canonical conclusion, and the zero-parameter theorem is its special case. MIIVsem remains the primary applied consumer of the exact audit. Inverting covariance confidence sets can use the audit as a subroutine, but that inferential layer is secondary and is not proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The mathematical proofs cover all singular Möbius branches on the fan-in-one side, every gate, repeated input, copy equation, covariance slot, and selector branch on the hard side, and the complete-fiber padding used for the fixed-\(k\) obstruction. The padded graph has maximum directed indegree at most three; equality is not claimed because an input may contain no two-parent sink. The presolve computations remain bounded sanity checks rather than an independently audited implementation or machine-checked proof. Certificates are deliberately componentwise quadratic because a single global primitive element can have exponential degree. Numerical stability near poles, approximate covariance input, and finite-sample coverage are outside the exact rational-covariance theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The central exact claims are fully discharged: the fan-in-one real fiber is equivalent to the pole-aware Möbius and \(2\)-CNF normalization, the planted-selector source language has the stated promise completeness, and the private-parent compiler is bijective on the entire compiled coefficient fiber. The indegree-two hard family has directed depth one, maximum directed outdegree one, and directed weak components of size at most three. A further exact-fiber padding yields a hard family of maximum directed indegree at most three with \(K_G=0\), proving completeness for every fixed literal bound \(K_G\le k\); the zero-parameter theorem is only the \(k=0\) specialization of this broader result. Remaining audit limitations concern implementation and external verification, not open steps in those proofs: the bounded symbolic checks do not exhaust all rational inputs, and no machine-checked formalization or comprehensive literature audit is claimed. The theorem assumes an exact rational positive-definite covariance and does not establish finite-sample inference, conditioning guarantees near singular strata, covariance-confidence-set coverage, or an exact latent-to-observed fiber bijection. MIIVsem is the intended primary numerical-identification consumer; confidence-set inversion is secondary.

statement_notes.justification: The parameter \(K_G\) counts vertices of indegree exactly two, so the fiber-preserving padding makes it zero by turning each two-parent in-star into a three-parent in-star. The resulting \(K_G=0\) hard family lies in \(K_G\le k\) for every fixed nonnegative \(k\), yielding the stated uniform completeness conclusion.
statement_notes.gap: This resolves the literal parameterized question negatively without a genericity assumption. The separately displayed zero-two-parent hardness theorem should be read as the \(k=0\) special case, not as an independent discovery.
statement_notes.consumer: This is the canonical parameterized maximality result for the residual-algebra discussion; MIIVsem remains the paper's primary applied numerical-identification consumer.

proofs.proof_tex:
By the definition of \(K_G\), one has \(K_G\in\mathbb N_0\).  Hence
\[
K_G\le 0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_G=0.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{thm:few\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}parameter\mbox{-}hardness}\) with the fixed value \(k=0\).  Its completeness assertion and the displayed equivalence show that the literal parameterized class at \(k=0\) belongs to promise \(\forall\mathbb R\) and is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard.

For the more precise bounded-fan-in assertion, let
\[
\mathcal R_0
=\bigl\{(G,\Sigma,e)\text{ in the promise domain of }\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3:K_G=0\bigr\}.
\]
The same fixed-parameter theorem states that its hardness reduction lands in \(\mathcal R_0\); in particular, the corrected padding has maximum directed indegree at most three, as required by \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\).  Thus \(\mathcal R_0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hard.  Moreover, \(\mathcal R_0\) is a restriction of the literal \(K_G\le0\) promise class, which the fixed-parameter theorem places in \(\forall\mathbb R\).  Restricting the promise domain does not change the deciding predicate on the retained inputs, so the same universal-real decision procedure proves \(\mathcal R_0\in\forall\mathbb R\).  Consequently,
\[
\mathcal R_0\text{ is promise }\forall\mathbb R\text{-complete}.
\]

It remains to spell out the algorithmic consequence.  Suppose the residual-algebra handle of \(\mathrm{def:parameterized\mbox{-}handle}\) yielded an exact decision algorithm with running time \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) on the stated literal class.  On \(\mathcal R_0\), its running time would be
\[
f(K_G)\operatorname{poly}(n)=f(0)\operatorname{poly}(n).
\]
If \(N\) is the total binary input length, then \(n\le N\), so this is polynomial in \(N\).  It would therefore decide the promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete problem \(\mathcal R_0\) in polynomial time.  The fixed-parameter theorem's complexity consequence then gives \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  Contrapositively, unless that equality holds, \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) cannot yield the asserted fixed-parameter algorithm.

Finally, the hard family in the fixed-parameter theorem is obtained through an equality of complete coefficient fibers and not by deleting exceptional solutions.  Therefore its \(k=0\) specialization preserves singular branches and uses no genericity assumption, which proves the last sentence of the present theorem.

proposed.statement: For the parameter \(K_G\) as defined, the literal parameterized problem is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete already at \(k=0\).  More precisely, the restriction of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) to the instances satisfying \(K_G=0\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  Hence \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) cannot yield an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) algorithm for the class stated in the question unless \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  This conclusion uses singularity-preserving fiber bijections and no genericity assumption.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The refreshed proof is the \(k=0\) specialization of the sharpened fixed-parameter theorem, whose sibling-owned proof contains the corrected exact-fiber padding argument.  The dependency replacement records that direction explicitly and removes the obsolete independent derivation.
